results.title: How Agencies Find AI Search Visibility Gaps for Clients 2026
results.content:
Use a shared topic set (“best,” “vs,” “pricing,” “alternatives,” “near me”) and compare mentions/citations, sources AI uses, and the formats competitors win with.

Look for brand mentions without citations or citations pointing to third parties. Fix by publishing clearer source pages, improving schema, and adding original data AI can reference.

Audit pages for weak answer-first structure, missing entities, and lack of proof. Rewrite with clear summaries, comparisons, and scannable evidence so AI can extract and cite it.

## Conclusion [...] ### SEO & Content Audits

Start with Google Search Console to spot what rankings won’t show. Pages with high impressions but low CTR usually mean the snippet isn’t earning the click, the page doesn’t match intent, or SERP features are absorbing demand.

➡️ Compare competitors with Wellows, Ahrefs, or Semrush to find the topics and page types they win on, especially pricing, comparisons, and evaluation content.

Did you know?

Semrush’s AI Overviews research, based on analysis of over 10 million keywords, shows how visibility and click behavior shifts as generative answers appear more often in results (Search Engine Land, 2025).

Agency fix: map each priority page to one intent stage (informational, comparison, evaluation, purchase). Without that, traffic does not equal intent. [...] The agencies that win in the AI search era won’t be the ones chasing more traffic. They’ll be the ones who master how agencies find hidden AI search visibility gaps and turn those gaps into predictable revenue outcomes.

results.title: Search Agent Optimization: How to Boost Your AI Search Visibility
results.content:
That’s the new reality of search. Search Agent Optimization (SAO) means shaping your content so AI agents can easily pick it up, trust it, and share it as the best answer.

Search agents are AI-powered tools that gather and summarize information directly for users. They include chatbots built into search engines (think Bing Chat and Google’s Gemini), voice assistants like Alexa+, and even virtual research assistants that scour the internet behind the scenes.

Unlike traditional Google searches, these agents don’t simply index links—they interpret and package information into straightforward answers. [...] But the agents we're dealing with here? Totally different vibe. Less "evil villain bent on humanity's destruction," and more "helpful, slightly nerdy librarian who happily hands your content to your ideal customers."

## what is Search Agent Optimization (SAO)?

Search Agent Optimization (SAO) is the process of structuring and refining your content so AI tools—like ChatGPT, Bing Copilot, or Google SGE—can easily find, understand, and cite it in their answers. SAO helps your brand stay visible in AI-driven search results, even when users never click a traditional link.

Think about it like this: Instead of typing into Google and scrolling through page upon page of links, your customer asks an AI assistant like ChatGPT or Siri—and instead, they get one neat and tidy answer. [...] ### 1. make your website fast and AI-accessible

Think of AI agents as your most impatient visitors. They’ll bail if your page doesn't load instantly or if key content is buried in fancy scripts.

Aim for lightning-fast pages—sub-1-second response if you can. Compress images, use caching, and ditch bloated code.

Also, keep things simple. Many AI crawlers can't handle JavaScript well. Test your page’s raw HTML (Ctrl+U). If your content’s invisible there, it's probably invisible to bots, too. Keep critical info static or provide fallback content.

### From insight to content: Running the full AEO cycle

A content strategy for AI search has a natural architecture. Understand where you're not visible, find the prompts driving that gap, identify the citation sources you're missing, and create the content that fills those gaps. The problem a lot of teams hit is that the cycle lives in too many places—visibility data in one tool, prompt research in another, content production in a third—and the handoffs between them eat the velocity. [...] Profound empowers you to execute the full AEO cycle. The same platform that surfaces your citation gaps and query fan-out data also runs the content pipeline. A team using Agents typically starts in Answer Engine Insights or Prompt Volumes, identifies a prompt cluster where competitors are earning citations and they're not, and feeds that directly into an Agent as the brief. The AI Agent for content creation gathers citations, analyzes the top-performing pages for those prompts, conducts deep research, and produces a structured first draft.
